questions.questionText: Explain two characteristics that show that an organism is living. Give one example of a living organism.
questions.explanation: A characteristic is accepted when it is stated and appropriately explained.

questions.questionText: Describe the functions of the root, stem and leaf in a flowering plant.
questions.explanation: Functions should be matched to the correct plant parts.

questions.questionText: State two conditions necessary for successful seed germination and explain why each is needed.
questions.explanation: Any two correct conditions with explanations are acceptable.

questions.questionText: Construct a simple four-organism food chain using a green plant, a herbivore, a carnivore and a decomposer. Explain the direction of energy flow.
questions.explanation: Arrows should show feeding/energy transfer in the correct direction.

questions.questionText: Describe evaporation, condensation and precipitation as stages of the water cycle.
questions.explanation: Each stage must be correctly described.

questions.questionText: Explain the main role of the respiratory system and describe how oxygen reaches the blood.
questions.explanation: The answer should link breathing, lungs and gas exchange.

questions.questionText: Give three ways of preventing the spread of infectious diseases in a community and explain each.
questions.explanation: Any three appropriate measures with explanations.

questions.questionText: Describe how to make a simple electric circuit using a cell, wires, a switch and a bulb. Explain what happens when the switch is opened.
questions.explanation: The key idea is a complete conducting path.

questions.questionText: Explain friction and give two useful examples and one disadvantage of friction.
questions.explanation: Examples must clearly relate to friction.

questions.questionText: Name four weather instruments and state what each measures.
questions.explanation: Accept four correctly matched instruments and measurements.

questions.questionText: Compare renewable and non-renewable energy sources. Give two examples of each.
questions.explanation: The comparison must distinguish replenishment/finite supply.

questions.questionText: Explain the difference between transparent, translucent and opaque materials and give one example of each.
questions.explanation: Definitions and examples should match.

questions.questionText: Explain how sound is produced and how it travels from a vibrating source to a listener.
questions.explanation: The response should mention vibration and a medium.

questions.questionText: Explain the difference between input and output devices and give three examples of each.
questions.explanation: Examples must be correctly classified.

questions.questionText: State four safe practices when using the internet and explain why each is important.
questions.explanation: Any four well-explained practices.

questions.explanation: Formula and purpose should be clear.

questions.explanation: Any three valid record types.

questions.questionText:
(a) Name the pathogen and vector that cause bilharzia. [2 marks]
(b) State two ways a rural school can prevent bilharzia. [2 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Pathogen: Schistosoma blood fluke (flatworm). Vector/intermediate host: Freshwater snail [2 marks].
(b) Avoid swimming/wading in untreated slow-moving rivers; use safe borehole/piped water and proper toilets so eggs do not enter streams [2 marks].

questions.questionText: (a) Distinguish between a conductor and an insulator of electricity, giving one example of each. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: An electrical conductor allows electric current to pass through easily (e.g., copper wire or aluminium) [2 marks]. An insulator does not allow electric current to flow through it (e.g., dry plastic, rubber, or dry wood) [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
(a) State the three main methods of heat transfer. [3 marks]
(b) Give one everyday example of convection. [1 mark]
questions.explanation:
(a) Conduction, convection, and radiation [3 marks].
(b) Boiling water in a pot (warm water rises and cooler water sinks) or sea/land breezes [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
(a) Give two differences between sandy soil and clay soil. [4 marks]
(b) Explain why loam soil is best for growing maize. [2 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Sandy soil has large particles and drains water rapidly, whereas clay soil has very fine particles and holds water tightly (prone to waterlogging) [4 marks].
(b) Loam soil balances sand, silt, clay, and humus, giving good drainage, aeration, moisture retention, and nutrients [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
(a) List two input devices and two output devices of a computer. [4 marks]
(b) State one safe way to protect school computers from viruses. [1 mark]
questions.explanation:
(a) Input: keyboard, mouse, microphone, scanner. Output: monitor, printer, speakers [4 marks].
(b) Install updated antivirus software or avoid opening unknown USB drives/attachments [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
(a) Define the term "balanced diet". [2 marks]
(b) Name the deficiency disease caused by lack of protein in children and give one symptom. [2 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) A balanced diet contains all seven food nutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre, and water) in the correct proportions [2 marks].
(b) Kwashiorkor; symptoms include a swollen belly/feet (oedema), reddish thin hair, and peeling skin [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
(a) Explain how a solar panel produces electricity for a rural clinic. [2 marks]
(b) Give two advantages of solar energy over firewood. [2 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Photovoltaic cells in the solar panel convert light energy from the sun directly into electrical energy [2 marks].
(b) Clean/does not cause indoor smoke pollution or respiratory illness; renewable and reduces deforestation [2 marks].

questions.questionText: (a) What are the three principles of Pfumvudza conservation agriculture? [3 marks]
questions.explanation: 1. Minimum soil disturbance (digging planting basins instead of deep ploughing). 2. Permanent soil cover / mulching with dry grass. 3. Crop rotation alternating cereals with legumes [3 marks].
